intro: Hakuto-R Mission 1 was the first Moon landing attempt by the Japanese company ispace. Launched on 11 December 2022, it took a slow, low-energy route out to 1.38 million km from Earth and entered lunar orbit on 21 March 2023. On 25 April 2023, passing a crater rim about 3 km high, its software rejected the altimeter and believed the lander had touched down while it was still about 5 km up. It ran out of propellant and fell near Atlas crater, in Mare Frigoris.

images.caption: A model of the HAKUTO-R lander shown at the International Astronautical Congress in 2022. It carried the UAE Rashid rover and the SORA-Q transformable robot.
NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter found the impact site the next day: at least four pieces of debris around 47.581 N, 44.094 E.
